text:
sqlpipe moves table data from Postgres to S3 in three stages. The reader process opens a connection to the source database and streams rows in batches. Each batch holds a fixed number of rows, so memory use stays constant for large tables. The converter receives each batch and turns it into a Parquet row group. The converter applies the column types of the source table to the schema of the Parquet file. The uploader writes the finished row groups to S3 as parts of one multipart object.

If the network fails or S3 returns a 5xx error, the uploader retries the part. After the last part, the uploader completes the multipart upload and S3 makes the object visible. The three stages operate at the same time and pass data through channels.
